chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Inventor claims and Tudie's claim to have written Blues for Jimmy
summary: Musicians claim to have invented the bowed bass and mute, and Tudie claimed to have written a piece actually from Lucia.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I was just thinking. Tudie told me that he was the one that invented the bowed bass, George Foster told me he invented the bowed bass...
I mean, they all invented the bowed bass!
I think Ory invented the mute...
Yeah, yeah, and Zutty invented the bar (?)s and all that.
All these guys has got them things that they invented. They're a laugh a minute!
Tell me about when Ory came to make that record of "Blues For Jimmy," and Tudie claimed that he'd written it...
What it actually is, it was the sextet from Lucia De L'Amour, see.

See, he claimed he wrote it. And he says, "I want to get extra money for it" -- on this session. And Ory said, "You wrote no such thing." And Bud Scott said, "No, he wrote it." They'd say whatever you said or something.
Yeah, that's the sextet from Lucia.
He says, "I wrote the thing, and I want extra money.

I've heard lots of guys... I won't name names on paper. I've heard lots of New Orleans musicians claim they wrote the most outrageous things! Things that have been Classical pieces from Puccini and Verdi and all, and they said, "I wrote that, and they stole it from me." Tudie told me the same thing: "Well, I didn't (?)." But how could they steal that from him? That's been in the Classics for... But I mean, why do you think they ever got into such a state of mind, where they thought they could fool anybody into thinking they wrote that?
It's a hard thing to believe. You just imagine things, Barry, and then they repeat it so many times, that's... If repeat something long enough, then you
think it's got to be true.
